insights.title: Poor Sleep Linked to Prolonged Fatigue Streak
insights.body: Correlation: The 9-day elevated Tired and Meh streak (2026-07-29 – 2026-08-06) overlaps closely with the period surrounding the sleep outlier of 2h on 2026-07-28, the minimum for the entire 60-day range. Hypothesis: The extreme sleep deprivation on 2026-07-28 may have triggered or deepened the fatigue cluster that followed, given that sleep averaged 6.79h overall with a sd of 1.01h, making 2h a severe deviation of nearly 5 standard deviations. Correlation: Walking also shows its longest gap of 9 days spanning 2026-07-28 – 2026-08-05, perfectly mirroring the fatigue window, suggesting that reduced movement and poor mood reinforced each other during this stretch.
insights.confidence_reason: The 9-day Tired/Meh peak streak is the longest in the dataset and aligns precisely with the single worst sleep outlier (2h on 2026-07-28), but causation cannot be confirmed from sketch-level data alone.

insights.title: Recent Lighter Meals Coincide With Mood Improvement
insights.body: Correlation: The last-7d average for meal heaviness dropped sharply to 2.14 from a prior-7d average of 2.86, a trend delta of -0.71 — the largest trend movement of any numeric metric in the dataset. Correlation: Over that same last-7d window, the Tired vibe fell to 0 days of 'Often/A lot' compared to 14 peak tired days logged between 2026-07-29 and 2026-08-08, and positive moods (Calm: 3 Often days, Energized: 3 Often days) rebounded. Hypothesis: Consistently lighter meals in the most recent week may be contributing to reduced fatigue and improved mood, though shared confounders such as sleep (last-7d avg 6.73h, near the overall mean of 6.79h) cannot be ruled out.
insights.confidence_reason: The meal heaviness trend delta of -0.71 is nearly half the metric's sd of 1.47, representing a meaningful shift, and it co-occurs with a clear mood rebound, though n=60 daily observations limits causal inference.

insights.title: Weight Spike in Mid-July Was a Temporary Outlier
insights.body: Correlation: Five consecutive days from 2026-07-13 to 2026-07-17 registered as weight outliers above 1.5 standard deviations (180.8 to 181.6 lbs), all well above the 60-day mean of 179.67 lbs and sd of 0.69 lbs. Correlation: By 2026-08-13 and 2026-08-16, weight had swung to the opposite extreme with outliers at 178.5 and 178.6 lbs, and the last-7d average of 178.91 lbs sits 0.76 lbs below the overall mean, suggesting a full reversal of the mid-July spike. Hypothesis: The mid-July weight elevation may have been a transient fluctuation — possibly fluid or dietary — rather than a lasting change, as the overall trend across the period is only -0.11 lbs week-over-week.
insights.confidence_reason: With n=60 weight entries and a tight sd of 0.69 lbs, the 5-day cluster of outliers peaking at 181.6 lbs (nearly 3 sd above mean) followed by a return below mean is statistically clear and well-sampled.

insights.title: Breathing and Stretches Consistency Is Slipping
insights.body: Correlation: Breathing has a 60-day completion of 62% but its longest gap was 5 days (2026-08-01 – 2026-08-05), and Stretches has a 60-day completion of 63% with a last-7d completion dropping to just 43%, its longest gap running 4 days through 2026-08-14 – 2026-08-17. Hypothesis: Both habits appear to be declining in adherence most recently — Stretches' last-7d completion of 43% is well below its 60-day average of 63%, suggesting a recent drop-off rather than a stable low baseline. Correlation: This recent decline in movement-related habits (Walking at 60% overall, Stretches at 43% last-7d) coincides temporally with the late-July to early-August fatigue and Meh cluster, though the direction of influence is unclear.
insights.confidence_reason: Stretches' last-7d completion of 43% versus its 60-day average of 63% is a notable 20-percentage-point gap, though habit completion data lacks the numeric precision of continuous metrics to confirm a sustained trend.

insights.title: Water Intake Is Consistently Low Across the Period
insights.body: Correlation: Water intake was logged n=283 times over 60 days (roughly 4-5 entries per day), with a mean of 13.02 oz per entry and a median of 16 oz, but the minimum was just 4 oz on 2026-06-20 — the same day as the maximum of 24 oz, indicating high within-day variability (sd=7.73 oz). Hypothesis: With a last-7d average of 12.61 oz per entry trending slightly down (-0.27) from the prior-7d average of 12.88 oz, hydration may be gradually declining, which could be a contributing factor to the recent fatigue signals, though the sketch data does not allow direct pairing of water entries with mood timestamps.
insights.confidence_reason: The water intake trend delta of -0.27 oz is very small relative to the sd of 7.73 oz, making it difficult to distinguish a real decline from normal day-to-day noise across the 283 logged entries.
